market_context: S&P 500 futures were up roughly 0.2% and Dow futures up 0.3%, while Nasdaq futures were approximately flat before the open.[1] Investors are focused on elevated Treasury yields, semiconductor weakness, and the 14:30 ET CPI release, with forecasts for headline CPI of 0.6% month-over-month and core CPI of 0.2%; the Beige Book is due at 20:00 ET.[4][10]

predictions.reasoning: S&P 500 futures were approximately 0.2% higher before the open, indicating modest positive breadth despite recent weakness.[1] The gain is likely to fade or remain limited if CPI reinforces the elevated-yield and hawkish-Fed concerns weighing on equities.[4][10]

Nasdaq futures were flat while semiconductor stocks remained under pressure, including a reported sharp decline in Applied Materials and broader memory-sector selling.[1][2][3] Elevated yields and potentially firm core CPI create greater downside sensitivity for long-duration technology shares.[4][5]

The semiconductor complex was a major source of overnight selling, with investors concerned about memory demand and uncertain chip-equipment spending.[2][3] A firm inflation reading could lift yields further and pressure high-valuation AI and semiconductor shares.[4][5]

Nasdaq futures were subdued despite stronger Dow and S&P futures, suggesting limited support for growth-sensitive megacaps at the open.[1][8] Tesla is exposed to the same valuation and interest-rate pressure affecting technology stocks if CPI raises expectations for additional Fed tightening.[4][5]

Dow futures gained about 0.3%, outperforming flat Nasdaq futures and pointing to relative strength in more economically mature and value-oriented constituents.[1] Positive premarket bank interest and strength in energy-linked shares may help the Dow outperform if rates remain elevated.[2][9]
